_note: ALL NUMBERS ARE PLACEHOLDERS for gameplay. Orbit period and eclipse time are rough figures and must be verified.
name: Earth Imager
goal_text: Take photos of coastlines for 12 weeks and get them to the ground.
blurb: Your first real mission. A camera, a radio and a lot of rules to balance.
teaches: Mass, power, data, money and time all pull against each other.

craft_values._note: Earth Imager only, per CubeSat size. mass_kg, power_w (most power the craft can make) and data_kbps come from the team values sheet (Values.pdf); the weekly data goal scales with data_kbps. bus_power_w (1U) and budget_k (6U) are game placeholders so every size has a 3-star design.

requirements.reason: The spacecraft is heavier than the rocket slot allows.
requirements.tip: Remove a part or swap for a lighter one.
requirements.consequence: The launch provider refuses an overweight spacecraft, so you cannot launch.

requirements.text: Deliver at least 40 MB of photos per week
requirements.reason: The radio sends less than the mission needs.
requirements.tip: Add a big antenna or a second ground station.
requirements.consequence: Fewer photos reach the ground each week.

requirements.reason: The parts use almost all the power the panels make.
requirements.tip: Use larger panels or a part that needs less power.
requirements.consequence: With no spare power, the battery drains a little every week.

requirements.text: Keep at least 10% of the budget in reserve
requirements.reason: There is too little money left for surprises.
requirements.tip: Choose cheaper parts or finish building sooner. Every day costs money.
requirements.consequence: A surprise cost in orbit can cancel the mission.

requirements.reason: The battery is too small to last through the dark part of the orbit.
requirements.tip: Add a battery or a larger one.
requirements.consequence: The satellite browns out in every eclipse and loses data. With no battery it dies.

requirements.reason: Building and testing took too long.
requirements.tip: Build faster. Each retest also adds days.
requirements.consequence: You miss your launch slot and pay to rebook a later one.

rocket.name: Delta 900
rocket.why: NASA's workhorse Delta, with strap-on boosters.

differences: The first satellite built to photograph Earth's land. Its scanner sent back hundreds of thousands of pictures of farms, forests and coastlines.
A camera mission: photos are big files.
Plenty of time (launch by day 180) and money.

based_on.story: The first satellite built to photograph Earth's land. Its scanner sent back hundreds of thousands of pictures of farms, forests and coastlines.
based_on.lesson: A camera mission lives or dies by how much data it can get down.
